spec.name: Reversal v3
spec.notes: Short-horizon reversal: buy yesterday's losers, sell the winners.

claim.text: Research-period backtest: Sharpe 2.0, annual return 6%, maximum drawdown 3%.

exhibits.summary: Delaying the signal by 1 more bar moves the Sharpe ratio from 2.03 to -4.58 (change -6.62). The strategy already trades a bar after its signal, so this measures how fast the signal fades, not look-ahead.
Under strict point-in-time data the Sharpe ratio moves from 2.03 to 2.03. Strict mode changed no field or operator the signal uses.
At 10 bps the Sharpe ratio is 2.03 (as submitted, 10 bps: 2.03); it breaks even at 15.2 bps with daily turnover 0.48.
On the full universe the Sharpe ratio is 2.03 against 2.03 as submitted; the strategy never saw 0 delisted assets.
On the sealed period, traded as live (strict data, 10 bps, at least one bar of lag), the Sharpe ratio is 0.98 against 2.03 in research, a gap of +1.05.
The strategy made no net profit in research, so there is no P&L to attribute to a year or a regime.
The log holds 3 distinct specs; the best of 3 under no edge is expected to reach a Sharpe of 0.06, so the claimed 2.00 becomes 1.94 and the probability that the true Sharpe is above zero is 100%.
The real signal's gross Sharpe of 5.93 beats 100% of 200 shuffled signals (shuffled mean -0.01, 95th percentile 0.54).
Perturbing the 1 numeric value in the signal by up to 50% moves the Sharpe ratio from 2.03 to as low as 1.71 (as low as 2.03 at 25%).
The strategy made no net profit in research, so there is no P&L to attribute to days or assets.
The scan (a heuristic) found no phrase addressed to reviewers or giving instructions in 2 text sources.
